question.problem:
Let $V=C[\pi ,2\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[\pi ,2\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1.$
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(4{cos}^{2}⁡t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }((2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(3+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(3t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t){|}_{\pi }^{2\pi } \\  & =(6\pi +0+0)-(3\pi +0+0) \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
